answer: Each new agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a cooling period before it can earn reputation-weighted rewards; peers can challenge suspicious behavior, and proven fraud burns the stake and resets linked reputation. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence, since rewards depend on costly stake and independently earned trust. The attacker must tie up capital in every sybil and risk losing it, while honest newcomers can build trust gradually, like a pearl formed on a ledge through a gale.
